subject: arts-music
essential_question: How can understanding portfolio, rehearsal, and exhibition help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Demonstrate current mastery of revision through selected-response, constructed-response, and applied evidence.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of revision.
Check, revise, or improve work about revision using stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about revision.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: This is day 11 of "Portfolio, Rehearsal, and Exhibition". That is unit 6 in grade 4. Today is an unit assessment about revision. It takes about 40–60 minutes. It is one day's work, not the whole unit project. Your unit is working toward this: Present a visual, musical, theatrical, dance, or mixed-media portfolio with process evidence, privately or publicly by choice. Today helps by working on revision. Your unit also covers selecting work, artist statements, rehearsal plans, and peer feedback. Today counts for a grade. Do it on your own.
primary_task: Do the unit task for revision on your own. Make what the task asks for. Show your process, not just the finished piece. Check it against the criteria before you hand it in. Then judge it yourself. What did you want? What did it really do? Where is the gap? Everything must be your own work. You never have to perform in public, use a camera, record your voice, or take a photo to pass. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about revision. It is part of "Portfolio, Rehearsal, and Exhibition". Later days in this unit cover other things, like selecting work. Before you stop, do this check: Rate confidence in revision, cite one piece of evidence from today, and choose: ready to extend, ready to review later, or need a different explanation. In grade 4, try the steps yourself before you ask for help. Give a reason in your own words for at least one choice. A labelled drawing or a spoken answer counts fully.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This work takes more than one sitting. Ask for a simple checklist with dates so you know what to do next. Keeping track is not part of your grade.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
No public performance, voice recording, photo, or camera use is ever required; provide a private, written, or no-audio alternative for every task.
Use only original student work, public-domain material, or properly licensed excerpts; never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or protected works.
The final product must remain the student’s own authorship; adult or AI assistance may support planning and feedback but must not create the graded work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting revision.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for revision follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for revision, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for revision works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of revision, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking revision mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply revision under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on revision rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
